summary:
When astronauts travel to Mars, sending a message back to Earth can take over twenty minutes. If a medical emergency happens, waiting for a doctor’s reply isn’t an option, the crew has to handle it themselves, even if none of them are physicians.

That’s why we built AURA (Autonomous Crew Resilience & Triage Engine). AURA is an intelligent medical cockpit designed specifically for non-doctors in deep space. Instead of overwhelming the crew with confusing numbers, it connects vital signs with spacecraft telemetry, Slike cabin CO2and radiation spikes—to pinpoint what’s actually going wrong. When something is off, AURA translates medical jargon into plain language and walks the crew through step-by-step emergency care, even pointing them to the exact physical medkit compartment to grab.

Because deep space has no internet, AURA runs 100% offline with encrypted verification to keep health records secure.

Best of all, this isn't just for space. Our 1G Remote Clinic mode brings the exact same offline guidance to community health workers in rural clinics back home in Ghana, helping save lives where doctors are hours away.
details:
How AURA Works & What It Does

When astronauts embark on multi-year journeys to Mars, Earth is up to 22 light-minutes away. Round-trip radio communication can take over 40 minutes, and most deep-space crews will not have an onboard doctor. When a medical crisis occurs, the crew cannot wait for Houston or ground control, they have to diagnose and treat it themselves.

AURA (Autonomous Crew Resilience & Triage Engine) is an autonomous medical cockpit built specifically for non-physician astronauts. Here is how it works:

  • Connects the Body to the Spacecraft: Rather than looking at vital signs in isolation, AURA cross-references human biometrics (heart rate, blood pressure, eye pressure, oxygen saturation) with cabin telemetry (carbon dioxide levels, solar particle radiation, cabin temperature). If an astronaut develops a pounding headache and elevated eye pressure, AURA detects that cabin CO2​ has crept past safe thresholds, pinpointing the real environmental root cause.
  • Adapts to Gravity: The human body changes drastically across different gravity fields. AURA automatically shifts its medical warning baselines whether the crew is floating in 0G Transit, walking on the 1/6G Moon, working in 3/8G Mars, or back on 1G Earth.
  • Plain-Language Non-Doctor Guidance: In an emergency, non-medical astronauts do not have time to decipher clinical jargon. AURA translates complex anomalies into three simple questions: What changed?, Why does it matter?, and What should we do right now?
  • 3-Tap Emergency Responder: With just three quick taps, AURA opens an emergency guide with visual timers and directs the crew to the exact physical locker and drawer in their onboard medical kit (for example, Medical Rack Bay B2, Drawer 4).

What Makes It Creative

Most health dashboards simply display graphs and sound generic alarms when numbers spike. AURA does something completely different:

  1. Interactive Anatomical Twin: An interactive 3D and 2D visual twin highlights affected organs in real time, letting astronauts visually see where physiological stress is occurring.
  2. Context-Aware Diagnosis: Instead of treating symptoms blindly, AURA links human physiology directly with life support data so the crew treats the actual cause.
  3. Physical-to-Digital Bridge: Every medical instruction ties directly to physical stowage compartments and medkit bay IDs, eliminating frantic searching during a crisis.

Key Factors Our Team Considered

  • Extreme Crew Stress & Cognitive Overload: During an alarm, adrenaline is high. We designed the interface with clean, glanceable cards, high-contrast typography, and zero clutter. Every critical action is reachable in three taps or fewer.
  • Communication Blackouts & Zero-Internet Reality: Deep space offers no cloud servers. AURA operates 100% offline in the browser. All sensor packets are sealed with SHA-256 cryptographic hashes and queued in an offline vault, ensuring medical records remain private, untampered, and ready to sync whenever ground contact resumes.
  • Medical Safety & Non-Doctor Safeguards: AURA never makes up medical advice. It strictly follows NASA flight health standards (NASA-STD-3001) and includes built-in safety checks to prevent incorrect drug dosages or dangerous contraindications.

Intended Impact: From Deep Space to Rural Earth

  • In Space: AURA gives long-duration crews the autonomy, confidence, and clinical capability to survive missions beyond low-Earth orbit without needing a dedicated flight surgeon on board.
  • On Earth (Dual-Use Spin-Off): We designed AURA with our own communities in mind. In 1G Remote Clinic Mode, community health workers in rural villages across Ghana and other underserved regions, where doctors are miles away and internet is unreliable, can use AURA completely offline on a basic tablet or laptop to deliver life-saving first-response triage.

Tools, Languages & Technologies Used

  • Frontend Framework: Next.js (React) with TypeScript for a reliable, rock-solid codebase.
  • Styling & Design System: Tailwind CSS, built with a custom avionics color system (Inter and Sora typography, high-contrast clinical status tokens).
  • Data Visualization & 3D Twin: Recharts for smooth trend analysis, and Three.js / custom responsive SVG for the interactive anatomical twin.
  • Offline Resilience & Security: Local browser IndexedDB storage for the offline vault and Web Crypto API (SHA-256) for data integrity.
  • NASA Open Data & Flight Standards: Seeded with physiological and environmental datasets from the NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) (studies OSD-379, OSD-137, OSD-53, and RadLab ISS telemetry), and aligned with NASA-STD-3001 and NASA Spacecraft Maximum Allowable Concentrations (SMAC).
